transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I came in because I just feel really low most days. Like I’m sitting at the bottom of some dark hole and I can’t get out of it. Even when I’m around people I know, it’s still there, this heavy, hopeless feeling.

Sorry, I know that sounds dramatic. I work with my hands, fixing things, and usually if something’s broken you can find the part or the wire or whatever, but with this I just… I don’t know where to start.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?

Yeah… it did. It’s been about a year and, what, two months now. It started after I had that fall on an HVAC job back in the fall and hurt my back.

I keep thinking if I’d just stepped different, or if the ladder had been set a little better… I don’t know. After that, everything kind of started unraveling. One thing led to another, and I never really got back to feeling like myself.
Have you felt this low most days for at least two years?

No… not two years. It’s been more like about a year and two months. It really started after that fall on the HVAC job, when I messed up my back, and then everything just kind of… went sideways from there. I mean, I keep measuring time by before the fall and after the fall now, which is not how I used to think about things, but yeah—not quite two years.
Do you feel your low mood is mainly about the fallout from your back injury?

I… I don’t know if I can say it’s mainly that. The back injury was definitely where things seemed to start coming apart, but then it’s hard to separate what’s from that and what’s just… me getting stuck in it, I guess.

It’s like when one thing breaks in a unit and then it puts strain on everything else, you know? Sorry, that’s probably not the clean answer you’re looking for. I guess what I know is the fall set something off, but I’m not sure it explains all of this.
Do you feel your depression would still be this strong if the problems from the back injury were no longer part of your life?

I think… yeah, maybe it would. I mean, the back stuff is part of it, sure, but I came in because most days it feels like I’m sitting at the bottom of this dark hole. Even if I’m around people I know, like family or folks I should feel normal with, I still can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling.

It’s funny—not funny, but… I used to be the one people called when something broke, you know? I could figure things out, get moving. Now it’s like that feeling just sits on me no matter what’s happening around me. So I don’t think taking the injury problems away would just make this disappear.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… yeah, I have. I used to love hiking, when my body would let me get out there, and painting, and going to the makerspace to tinker with stuff. Even just figuring out a tricky install used to give me this little spark, like, okay, I know how to solve this.

Now I’ll sit there and look at the paint or the tools or whatever, and I just… don’t start. Or someone from the makerspace calls and I let it ring because I can’t make myself care enough to go. It all feels like too much trouble, or like there’s no point to starting.
Before this started after your fall, had you ever gone through another period where you felt this same kind of depression?

I’m not sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, everybody has bad stretches, right? I’ve had times where I was down or worn out, especially when work was rough or life got messy, but I don’t know if I’d call it the same as this.

Before the fall, I was still… functioning, I guess. I’d get up, go to work, deal with whatever needed fixing. I remember one winter where everything at the shop kept breaking and I was just dragging, and then my sister kept telling me I looked tired—sorry, that’s probably not what you asked.

I don’t know. I can’t point to another time that felt exactly like this.
Along with feeling depressed, have you been feeling anxious or on edge a lot?

I don’t know… anxious, like worried all the time? I mean, I get wound up about things, sure, but sometimes I can’t tell if that’s anxiety or just me being tired of everything.

Like, the other day I was trying to find this one receipt in a drawer and ended up cleaning out half the kitchen junk drawer, and then I forgot why I started—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. I guess I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m “on edge” exactly. Mostly I just feel… low.
Before the fall, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?

Before the fall… I’m not sure. I mean, I came in now because most days it feels like I’m sitting at the bottom of some dark hole, and even if I’m around people I know, I still can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling.

Before that, I had rough patches, sure, but I don’t know if it was nearly every day for two weeks like you’re asking. It’s hard for me to pin it down.
Have you been worrying a lot lately?

I don’t really know how to measure “a lot.” I mean, I worry about normal things, I guess—bills, getting things done, whether I forgot something at the store… actually yesterday I went in for detergent and came out with light bulbs and no detergent, which about sums me up lately.

But if you mean sitting there constantly thinking something bad is going to happen, I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it that way. Mostly I just feel kind of weighed down.
Before the fall, was there ever a time in your life when you lost interest in things you usually enjoy for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I used to really love hiking, and painting, and going down to the makerspace to tinker with stuff. Even at work, figuring out a tricky install used to kind of… I don’t know, wake my brain up a little.

But now I’ll look at the paint or the tools and just… stare at them. Or I ignore calls from people asking if I want to go do something, because none of it feels worth even starting. I guess that has gone on for more than a couple weeks.
Before your fall, was there ever a time when you felt down or hopeless nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of why I came in. Most days I feel like I’m sitting at the bottom of this dark hole, and even if I’m around people I know—like, people who are trying to be normal with me or cheer me up—I still can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling.

Before the fall, though… I’m getting tangled up in the timeline. It all sort of blurs together, like when you’re trying to remember which job site had the bad wiring and which one had the leaky ceiling. But the feeling itself, yeah, it’s been there most days.
Before your fall, was there ever a time when depression clearly lasted at least two weeks and then got better for a while?

I’m not sure I can separate it out that cleanly. Like… “clearly lasted two weeks and then got better” sounds neat, and it doesn’t feel neat in my head.

There were times I thought maybe I was doing better, like I’d get through a week of work and think, okay, maybe I’m getting a handle on it, and then something dumb would throw me off—like losing a tool I had just set down, which I swear happens constantly at job sites, even when you’re not feeling like this. One time I spent twenty minutes looking for a level and it was in my back pocket.

So… I don’t know. I can’t really point to a clean stretch where it ended and I was fine for a while. It’s more blurry than that.
Before the fall, did you ever have a period of depression that clearly got better before this current depression began?

I don’t know if I can say it clearly got better, no. I’m trying to think of it like… like before this current stretch, was there some obvious break where I was okay again, and I just can’t pin that down.

It’s more like when a machine is making a bad noise and sometimes it quiets down, so you think maybe it fixed itself, but then it starts up again and you realize it was still there the whole time. I had days where I could get through things better, sure, but I don’t know that I’d call that “better” in the way you mean.
Before your fall, was there ever a time when you were clearly back to your usual self for at least two months?

Two months… I don’t know. I mean, “usual self” is hard to measure, isn’t it? Like, I know what I used to be like, more or less, but trying to point to a clean two-month stretch before the fall where I was definitely back there… I can’t really say that.

There were patches where I probably seemed more normal from the outside. I’d go to work, do what needed doing, talk to people. But two whole months where I could say, yes, I was back to myself? I’m not sure. It all kind of runs together when I try to look back at it.
Before this current depression, was there ever a time in your life when you were depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I mean, I came in because most days it feels like I’m sitting at the bottom of some dark hole. It’s not just a bad afternoon or being annoyed because something went wrong at work—though, you know, work can do that to anybody. One little thing breaks loose and suddenly the whole job’s backed up.

But this is different. Even if I’m around people I know, I still feel heavy, like hopeless in a way I can’t shake. So… nearly every day for two weeks? I think that’s probably yes, if that’s what you’re asking.
Before this current period started, was there ever a separate time in your life when you were depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I know I kind of said it already, but… yeah, I think so. It’s hard for me to separate it into neat “periods,” because when I look back it all blurs together.

But before this current stretch, there were definitely times when most days I felt like I was sitting at the bottom of some dark hole. Even if I was around people I knew, it didn’t really lift. That heavy, hopeless feeling would just stay there.

Sorry, I’m probably wandering off a bit. It’s just hard to put dates around it.
Before this current depression began, was there ever a time when you felt back to your normal self for at least two months?

I’m not really sure. I know you’re asking if there was a clean stretch where I was back to normal for two months, but I can’t pin that down.

There were times I functioned better, I guess—went to work, did the regular things, dealt with people—but whether that means I was actually “normal” again for two whole months… I don’t know. It all kind of blends together when I try to sort it out.
At any point in your life, have you gone at least two months without feeling depressed or hopeless?

I don’t know if I can honestly say that. I mean, there are days where I can get through work and talk to people, do what needs doing—like when something breaks and you just focus on the next part, the next tool, the next call—but that doesn’t mean the heaviness is gone.

Most days it feels like I’m down in this dark hole, and even when I’m around people I know, I still can’t really shake that hopeless feeling. So two whole months without that… I don’t think so.
Do you feel anxious or nervous much of the time?

I don’t know… maybe? I’m not sure I’d call it nervous exactly. I get wound up sometimes, like my body’s braced for something, but then I’m also just tired of everything, so it’s hard to tell what’s what.

At work, when a job goes wrong, you just sort of go into fixing mode, you know—check the panel, trace the problem, try not to think too much. I guess I’ve learned to do that with myself too, just keep moving. So… anxious much of the time? I’m not sure how to answer that.
